title: Pravda Replikanta — Engineering Edition
lead: Two new research methods: predicting motion and learning from failed actions.

news.title: WorldFlow forecasts video and 3D motion together
news.summary: The October 29 WorldFlow study predicts future video and 3D point trajectories; average displacement error on SpatialCog was 0.060 m.
news.details: The researchers trained the joint architecture on 1.44 million object-level samples. Their WorldFlowBench evaluation set contains 1,678 samples from 11 sources. On SpatialCog, average displacement error was 0.060 metres, a 54.2% reduction compared with the strongest external baseline in the authors' tests.
news.technical_novelty: Joint generative prediction of visual appearance and spatial dynamics.
news.engineering_impact: A possible input to robot planning, not a complete controller.
news.limitations: Prediction accuracy does not establish autonomous task success.
news.body:
Robots can plan more effectively if they anticipate how a scene will change. WorldFlow, reported on October 29, predicts both future video frames and the movement of selected points in three-dimensional space. This is a predictive world model, not a system that directly commands motors.

The researchers trained the joint architecture on 1.44 million object-level samples. Their WorldFlowBench evaluation set contains 1,678 samples from 11 sources. On SpatialCog, average displacement error was 0.060 metres, a 54.2% reduction compared with the strongest external baseline in the authors' tests.

A real deployment would still require latency measurement, camera calibration checks, occlusion robustness and analysis of accumulated error. Forecasting geometry accurately does not itself demonstrate safe or reliable manipulation.

news.title: Event2Reward learns from setbacks and recovery
news.summary: The October 29 study uses imperfect executions as learning signals; average success improved by 18.16 percentage points across 40 LIBERO tasks.
news.details: The authors analyzed approximately 100,000 real-robot execution records, including failures. They infer relative progress between nearby states instead of assigning absolute progress scores to every frame. Across 40 tasks in four LIBERO suites, average policy success improved by 18.16 percentage points against a sparse-reward baseline.
news.technical_novelty: Relative progress comparisons complement sparse end-of-task rewards.
news.engineering_impact: Failed attempts can provide useful training information.
news.limitations: Results are task-specific; safe industrial learning is unproven.
news.evidence_status: Research preprint with simulation and physical-robot experiments.
news.body:
A robot may keep moving while making no progress. Event2Reward, introduced on October 29, learns to distinguish stalls, setbacks and recoveries. The estimated progress helps shape rewards for reinforcement learning rather than relying only on final success labels.

The authors analyzed approximately 100,000 real-robot execution records, including failures. They infer relative progress between nearby states instead of assigning absolute progress scores to every frame. Across 40 tasks in four LIBERO suites, average policy success improved by 18.16 percentage points against a sparse-reward baseline.

On real robots after 30 minutes of training, average success reached 60% on three precision-insertion tasks and 90% on three object-manipulation tasks. These are author-reported results, not a guarantee of safe online learning in factories.
